links.claim: Hypothesis: FOXA1 binds the reference C allele preferentially and the T allele weakens binding; no direct allele-specific binding evidence exists.

PELI2 has cancer-relevant literature, but no specific breast-cancer phenotype for PELI2 at this variant is established.

grades_v0.reason: No evidence_ids are cited. There is no QBiC-SELEX, ChIP-seq, MPRA, or allele-specific binding data for FOXA1 at rs11629191. The claim that FOXA1 binds the C allele more strongly is unsupported, and FOXA1 was selected without any QBiC coverage/screen support; qbic_coverage is only 'not_checked'.

E03 supports only that no annotated cCRE overlaps the variant and that the nearest cCRE is a dELS 1868 bp away. It does not show a cryptic enhancer active in breast cancer cells, so the regulatory-element part of the claim is indirect.

E02 supports PELI2 as the nearest listed protein-coding gene, but at 230.8 kb it is a very distant candidate. E06a confirms that Pellino2 is a Pellino-family E3 ubiquitin ligase, but neither source establishes that this variant's element targets PELI2.
No evidence_ids are cited. Nothing shows FOXA1 or PELI2 mediates an effect in MCF7 or any breast cancer cell type for this variant.

E06 shows that Europe PMC returns 178 hits for 'PELI2 AND breast cancer', but the quoted abstracts do not establish a specific breast-cancer phenotype for PELI2. E06a is generic Pellino-family biology, E06b is thyroid carcinoma, and E06c/E06d do not concern PELI2. This is at most indirect cancer-relevant context.

No evidence_ids are cited. There is no allele-specific ESR1 binding evidence for rs11629191, and qbic_coverage is only 'not_checked'. The claim that ESR1 binds the T allele more strongly is unsupported.
E03 shows no cCRE overlaps the variant, which is consistent with invoking a cryptic element, but it provides no evidence for an estrogen-responsive distal enhancer in breast cancer cells.

E05 does report a molecular-QTL credible set containing the variant for ENSG00000259868, but with PIP 0.03 and in GTEx brain nucleus accumbens, not breast tissue. This is directly relevant only as a very weak, wrong-tissue QTL link.
No evidence_ids are cited. Nothing shows the ESR1/ENSG00000259868 effect occurs in MCF7 or breast cancer cells.
No evidence_ids are cited. There is no evidence that altered ENSG00000259868 expression affects breast cancer risk or progression.

grades_final.reason: No evidence ID is cited for allele-specific FOXA1 binding. The claim is explicitly a hypothesis; no QBiC-SELEX, allele-specific ChIP, MPRA or reporter data show FOXA1 binding at this position, let alone preferential binding of the reference C allele. The only FOXA1-related evidence in the case (E07) is an absence-of-peak statement in MCF7 and is not cited here; absence of an ENCODE peak does not demonstrate allele-specific binding. Also, qbic_coverage is 'not_checked' with no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for FOXA1 shown; a QBiC-SELEX lookup should be run before any binding direction is claimed.

E03 directly shows that no ENCODE v4 cCRE overlaps chr14:55887040 (nearest dELS EH38E1716463 is 1868 bp away, 0 cCREs within 500 bp), which supports the annotation-absence part of the claim. However, the interpretive part - that this is a functional 'cryptic distal element' - is not shown by any cited assay (no reporter, MPRA, or chromatin accessibility/contact data at the site). The link is therefore consistent-with but indirect.

E02 supports only that PELI2 is the nearest listed protein-coding gene at 230.8 kb upstream, and E06a supports that PELI2 encodes a Pellino E3 ubiquitin ligase. Neither establishes that any element at this variant targets PELI2: no chromatin contact, eQTL in breast tissue, or perturbation links the variant to PELI2. The chain's own caveat that element-to-gene targeting is unproven is accurate, so the gene link rests on proximity alone (weak).

No evidence ID is cited. Nothing in E01-E09 shows FOXA1 occupancy, allelic binding, or PELI2 regulation by this variant in MCF7 (DepM ACH-000019). E07 reports no FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF7-matching biosamples, which if anything is inconsistent with the proposed MCF7 mechanism and in any case is not cited for this link.

E06 shows that PELI2 has cancer literature (178 hits; E06b lists PELI2 among prognostic genes in papillary thyroid carcinoma), so 'PELI2 has cancer-relevant literature' is supported at a general level. But none of the quoted abstracts (E06a-E06d) establish a breast-cancer phenotype for PELI2, and none link PELI2 to rs11629191. The variant-specific, breast-cancer-specific phenotype claim is therefore indirect at best.

No evidence ID is cited for allele-specific ESR1 binding. The claim is explicitly a hypothesis; no QBiC-SELEX, allele-specific ChIP, MPRA or reporter data show ESR1 binding at this position or preferential binding of the alt T allele. E08 (absence of ENCODE ESR1 peaks in MCF7) is not cited and would not establish allele-specific binding anyway. qbic_coverage is 'not_checked' with no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for ESR1 shown; that lookup should be performed to check whether ESR1 is even in coverage and whether any predicted binding change exists.

E03 supports the annotation-absence part (no cCRE overlaps the variant; nearest dELS 1868 bp away), so the site is unannotated. But the specific claim that this is an 'estrogen-responsive element' has no cited support: no ESR1 ChIP, accessibility, or reporter data at the site. The functional element claim is therefore an inference rather than a demonstrated result.

E05 provides a single molecular-QTL credible set for ENSG00000259868 with PIP 0.03, from GTEx brain nucleus accumbens - a very low posterior probability and a tissue unrelated to breast cancer or MCF7. This is weak, indirect genetics consistent with a possible regulatory link but far from establishing that the variant regulates ENSG00000259868, and it does not connect to the proposed ESR1 mechanism. The chain's caveat that breast-tissue regulation is not established is accurate.

No evidence ID is cited. Nothing in E01-E09 shows ESR1 occupancy or allele-specific ESR1 activity at this position in MCF7, and E09 reports no significant GTEx v8 breast-mammary eQTL for the variant. The MCF7-specific ESR1 mechanism is unsupported.

No evidence ID is cited. E04 shows zero GWAS Catalog associations for rs11629191, E05's only credible set is a molecular QTL (no GWAS), E09 shows no breast-tissue eQTL, and ENSG00000259868 is not mentioned in the literature quotes. Nothing bears on the claim that altered ENSG00000259868 expression affects breast cancer risk or progression.

checks.why: Tests whether FOXA1 occupies the variant region in the relevant breast cancer cell line; a negative result strongly weakens chain_1 binding, while a peak would justify follow-up allele-specific assays.
Tests whether ESR1 occupies the variant region in MCF7; without an ESR1 peak, the alt-allele ESR1-binding hypothesis has no cell-type anchor.
Tests whether rs11629191 is an eQTL for ENSG00000259868 in breast tissue, which would directly address the wrong-tissue weakness of E05; if it is also a PELI2 eQTL, it informs H1.gene.
